resources.string: matching encrypted answers
usable encrypted answers
split tunnel bypass
Direct and proxied paths do not present the same network identity.
Route apps and domains through one path, then rerun the detection check.
Xray API access
A local API or outbound configuration was reachable from the device.
Restrict local API access and hide exported outbound metadata.
IP consensus mismatch
Observed public IPs diverge across detection channels.
Align DNS, proxy, VPN, and app routing so every checker sees the same exit.
IP comparison mismatch
Regional IP comparison probes saw inconsistent public identities.
Use one exit path for both local and remote comparison probes.
GeoIP or location conflict
GeoIP, SIM, or network-country signals do not agree.
Choose an exit region that matches the network context or disable mismatched routing.
Android VPN binding
Android network capabilities expose VPN routing to local observers.
Review VPN mode, per-app routing, and active VPN ownership before retesting.
local proxy
A local proxy endpoint is visible to detection probes.
Bind proxy listeners narrowly and avoid exposing local ports to checked apps.
installed or active app artifact
Installed package or active service metadata matches VPN or bypass tooling.
Hide app metadata where possible and disable unrelated active VPN services.
DNS observability
DNS resolver behavior differs from the expected encrypted or routed path.
Align direct, bootstrap, and encrypted DNS settings with the selected exit path.
TLS handshake traits differ from the expected browser-like profile.
Switch to a browser-like TLS profile and retest after reconnecting.
network observability
Network interface or routing metadata exposes a tunnel-shaped path.
Review MTU, interface, and routing settings for tunnel-specific markers.
timing anomaly
Latency or timing patterns differ from ordinary direct HTTPS traffic.
Try a closer exit, reduce chained hops, or select a lower-latency profile.
native runtime signal
Native checks found hook, root, or hidden-interface artifacts.
Remove unrelated instrumentation and retest on the target device profile.
call transport leak
Call or STUN transport probes reveal a different path than expected.
Route realtime transports through the same protected path as HTTPS traffic.
ICMP observability
ICMP probes need review for path or spoofing behavior.
Verify raw-path behavior and disable strategies that expose ICMP differences.
Round-trip timing suggests a route inconsistent with the claimed location.
Use an exit closer to the apparent region or avoid high-latency chains.
CDN pull signal
CDN pull probes observed address or TLS traits that need review.
Check CDN-facing DNS and TLS routing before rerunning the probe.
WebRTC leak
WebRTC behavior exposes an address or path outside the expected route.
Enable WebRTC protection or route WebRTC through the protected path.
direct device signal
Local direct checks found proxy or VPN artifacts.
Review active VPN ownership, proxy ports, and app-visible network state.
indirect device signal
Installed-app or service signals make the setup recognizable.
Disable unrelated VPN apps and reduce app-visible bypass metadata.
location signal
SIM, roaming, or network-country metadata needs review.
Retest on the target network and align the exit region with local context.
bypass probe
Bypass-specific probes found a visible local or remote path.
Review split routing and proxy exposure, then rerun the bypass check.
Additional diagnostic signals need review
Detection probes did not expose bypass, VPN, IP, DNS, TLS, timing, or native observability signals.
Keep the current profile and rerun after changing networks or profiles.
Keep probes clean and improve the masking profile before relying on stricter networks.
